title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f82r three panel records build a shared population or list separate topics
summary: GDT790 owns f82r's three complete prose records to three visible panels: upper panel with no labels, middle with one, lower communal pool with twelve. Freeze those panel boundaries and complete paragraphs, including the corrected starts in GDT242. One exploratory whole reading makes the first record introduce participants or a state, the second alter or qualify them, and the lower record distribute the result among its visible stations. A rival reads three independently owned topics. Require an overt written carry relation and a source-independent participant identity before choosing either. Increasing visible population or label counts alone do not show narrative succession; exact okal reuse across owners remains ambiguous under GDT792/GDT793. No token translation, paragraph-to-figure bijection, or new page follows from this proposal.

design.mechanism: cross-panel participant and result dependency in a complete three-record reading
design.unit: the three admitted f82r panel-owned complete paragraphs and their fixed local label inventories
design.contrast: one participant/state carried through all three records versus three independent panel topics
design.prediction: A progressive account must assign each complete record a compatible role and exhibit a written, independently constrained bridge from the upper record into the middle and lower records; an independent-topic account permits different subjects and requires no such bridge. If both fit the complete text under free reference choices, retain nonselection.
design.prior_blockers: GDT790 establishes panel ownership but no word meanings; GDT242 corrected paragraph coordinates; GDT792/GDT793 leave cross-owner okal semantics underdetermined. Panel order, crowding, and label density are insufficient.
